For Provisioned Throughput by Tokens, you can also cancel auto renew to prevent it from renewing when the current term ends.\\n\\n## Deleting a Provisioned Throughput\\n\\nWhen you delete a Provisioned Throughput, you can no longer invoke the model at the throughput level that you purchased. If you delete a Provisioned Throughput linked to a custom model,\\nthe custom model isn't deleted. To learn how to delete a custom model, see Delete a custom model.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nYou can't delete a Provisioned Throughput by Model Units with commitment before the commitment term is complete.\\n\\nTo learn how to delete a Provisioned Throughput, choose the tab for your preferred method, and then follow the steps:\\n\\n#### Using Console\\n\\n1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM identity that has permissions to use the Amazon Bedrock console. Then, open the Amazon Bedrock console at\\n   <https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock>.\\n2. Select **Provisioned Throughput** from the left navigation pane.\\n3. From the **Provisioned Throughput** section, select a Provisioned Throughput.\\n4. Choose **Delete** from the **Actions** dropdown menu.\\n5. The console displays a modal form to warn you that deletion is permanent. Choose\\n   **Confirm** to proceed.\\n6. The Provisioned Throughput is immediately deleted.\\n\\n#### Using API\\n\\nTo delete a Provisioned Throughput, send a DeleteProvisionedModelThroughput request with an Amazon Bedrock control plane endpoint. Specify either the name of the Provisioned Throughput or its ARN as the `provisionedModelId`. If deletion is successful, the response returns an HTTP 200 status code.\\n\\nSee code examples\\n\\n## Canceling auto renew for a Provisioned Throughput\\n\\nFor Provisioned Throughput by Tokens, you can cancel auto renew at any point before your commitment term ends to prevent a Provisioned Throughput from automatically renewing.\\n\\nIf you cancel auto renew, your Provisioned Throughput will remain in service until the end of your commitment term. If you need Provisioned Throughput after your current term expires, you will need to purchase a new Provisioned Throughput.\\n\\nTo learn how to cancel auto renew for a Provisioned Throughput by Tokens, choose the tab for your preferred method, and then follow the steps:\\n\\n#### Using Console\\n\\n1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM identity that has permissions to use the Amazon Bedrock console. Then, open the Amazon Bedrock console at\\n   <https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock>.\\n2. Select **Provisioned Throughput** from the left navigation pane.\\n3. From the **Provisioned Throughput** section, select a Provisioned Throughput.\\n4. Choose **Cancel auto renew** from the **Actions** dropdown menu.\\n5. For new applications, we recommend the bedrock-runtime endpoint.\\n\\n#### Using Messages API\\n\\n```\\nfrom anthropic import Anthropic\\nfrom aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token\\n\\ntoken = provide_token(region=\\\"us-east-1\\\")\\n\\nclient = Anthropic(\\n    base_url=\\\"https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/anthropic\\\",\\n    api_key=token,\\n)\\n\\nresponse = client.messages.create(\\n    model=\\\"global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7\\\",\\n    max_tokens=1024,\\n    messages=[{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?\\\"}]\\n)\\nprint(response)\\n```\\n\\n#### Using Responses API\\n\\n```\\nfrom openai import OpenAI\\n\\nclient = OpenAI()\\n\\nresponse = client.responses.create(\\n    model=\\\"global.openai.gpt-5.6-sol\\\",\\n    input=\\\"Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?\\\"\\n    )\\nprint(response)\\n```\\n\\n#### Using Chat Completions API\\n\\n```\\nfrom openai import OpenAI\\n\\nclient = OpenAI()\\n\\nresponse = client.chat.completions.create(\\n    model=\\\"global.openai.gpt-5.6-sol\\\",\\n    messages=[{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?\\\"}]\\n    )\\nprint(response)\\n```\\n\\n#### Using Converse API\\n\\n```\\nimport boto3\\n\\nclient = boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='us-east-1')\\nresponse = client.converse(\\n    modelId='anthropic.claude-opus-4-7',\\n    messages=[\\n        {\\n            'role': 'user',\\n            'content': [{'text': 'Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?'}]\\n        }\\n    ]\\n)\\nprint(response)\\n```\\n\\n#### Using Invoke API\\n\\n```\\nimport json\\nimport boto3\\n\\nclient = boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='us-east-1')\\nresponse = client.invoke_model(\\n    modelId='anthropic.claude-opus-4-7',\\n    body=json.dumps({\\n {"id": "bbd44bc3-0391-4888-b692-6a5f9189263f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Short answer: you can't exit the six-month commitment early. You can use the capacity, ask AWS for an exception, and make sure it ends cleanly in March.

**What the docs say about your situation**
- AWS documents that you can't delete a model-unit Provisioned Throughput with a commitment until the term is complete. Your `commitmentExpirationTime` of 2027-03-15 is about 16 weeks away.
- Billing is hourly and continues until you delete it. Idle time doesn't reduce the charge.
- The delete page says a committed Provisioned Throughput automatically renews at the end of each term. The documented "cancel auto renew" option (`disableAutoRenew` on `UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput`) is described only for Provisioned Throughput by Tokens. I couldn't confirm it applies to your model-unit purchase. Don't assume it will lapse on its own.
- The 12 empty days in your CloudWatch query don't point to a monitoring gap. Bedrock emits no datapoints when there are no invocations, so this matches your 6 invocations.

**Options**
1. **Run real traffic through it.** The hourly fee is fixed whatever you send, so any workload you move onto the provisioned model ARN costs nothing extra up to its capacity.
   - You could move dev/test, evals, batch jobs, internal tools or existing on-demand traffic for the same model onto it.
   - That recovers some on-demand spend you'd otherwise pay.
   - Check that your workload's model matches what the provisioned model serves.
2. **Ask AWS for a billing exception.** Open a Support case, or go through your account manager. The docs point to the account manager for model-unit questions. Explain the launch delay and ask for a credit, an early termination, or a conversion. Nothing in the docs promises this, so treat it as a request that may be declined.
3. **Let it run out and delete it cleanly.** If neither of the above works, delete it on or right after 2027-03-15. Before then, call `get-provisioned-model-throughput` and check whether the response shows an auto-renew setting. If it does, disable it now. If it doesn't, set a calendar reminder and a billing alarm for early March. A missed renewal would commit you to another six months.

I couldn't confirm whether you can reduce model units or change the commitment term mid-term, and I'd assume you can't. The modify page didn't load for me. Ask Support to confirm.

If the launch is only delayed, option 1 combined with option 2 is the most practical. Tell me which model it serves and what traffic you could move onto it, and I can help work out how much of the fee you could offset. I can also run read-only checks on the resource, including a pull of its Cost Explorer spend.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
